critical_code_review_comments: routes/trades.py _hydrate_trade_assets is called on all 4 endpoints exposed to the Transactions page (get_trades L1463, get_trade L1474, get_pending_trades L1493, get_league_trades L1524). Conditional-trades endpoint also hydrates. Nice single-source-of-truth.
Cap-hit fallback chain (contract.aav → _synthesize_player_salary → player.salary → 0) is robust — ensures the UI never shows a blank cap. Salary mirrors cap_hit so both card variants render.
Age is computed from birth_date when the flat 'age' field is missing on older seeds — good defensive coding. Falls back to 0 only if both are unavailable.
Pick assets are correctly skipped (asset_type=='pick' or item_type=='pick' or no player_id) — no fantasy fields leak onto picks, confirmed by test.
_STAT_CATEGORY_LABELS covers all standard NHL counting cats + goalie stats with human-friendly abbreviations; unknown keys fall back to Title Case which is fine.

Transactions.tsx correctly uses 'transactions.viewMode' localStorage key, initializes from stored value with try/catch, and persists on change. TradeCard + ConditionalAssetTable + ConditionalTradeCard all thread viewMode through consistently — no split-brain rendering.
Backwards-compat: pending tab filter includes status 'proposed'→'pending' normalization, verified live with the TFHL trade whose status is 'proposed' but which correctly renders in the Pending tab.

File-length note: /app/backend/routes/trades.py is 2257 lines and /app/frontend/src/lovable/pages/Transactions.tsx is 1266 lines — both above the 700-line threshold. Not a blocker for this iter but worth a future split (e.g., extract _hydrate_* helpers into routes/trade_hydration.py; extract TradeCard/ConditionalTradeCard into components/transactions/).
Transactions.tsx uses `// @ts-nocheck` — as noted in the request this is by design for the Lovable-scaffolded page; not flagged as an issue.
